summary: Twenty-five years of satellite fire data exist, but they don't add up. MODIS (since 2000) and VIIRS (since 2012) see fire differently. In our Australian Black Summer test, MODIS caught only 28 % of the small fires VIIRS detected, 74 % of raw detections were duplicates from multiple satellites, and adding NOAA-20 alone created 7,448 "new" fire cell-days. EmberSync turns all MODIS and VIIRS FIRMS products into one de-duplicated, calibrated cell-day record. It then gives any area a burning-activity calendar, cross-sensor agreement, new-ignition and escalation flags, and an intensity-gated surge alert. A back-cast model reconstructs VIIRS-equivalent activity from MODIS alone, cutting daily error from 60 % to 26 % out-of-time. That makes a consistent 2000→today record possible. The surge alert reached "High" 28 days before New South Wales' peak fire day. The whole 2-million-detection season runs in 9 seconds.
details:
https://pari-garayeva.github.io/embersync/

Users choose a region or draw a box on the map. EmberSync shows a daily calendar of harmonized burning activity, a stacked breakdown of what both sensors agree on and what only one sensor sees, a 4-level early-warning strip, and per-cell details: which satellites saw it, fused confidence, harmonized FRP, unique hotspots, and new-ignition or escalating status. The area's daily table exports as CSV.
